newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia regulator rejects Perdana deals.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia regulator rejects Perdana deals.

text.p: Malaysia's Perdana Industri Holdings Bhd, formerly Pengkalen Industrial Holdings, said its proposals to acquire three companies and issue equity were rejected by the Securities Commission for a second time.
The proposals were turned down once again by the Malaysian regulator on July 25, Commerce International Merchant Bankers said on behalf of the company.
The proposals were first rejected in September last year.

Perdana, which makes footwear, had proposed to acquire Choo Yeang Sdn Bhd, Choo Yeang Properties and Construction Sdn Bhd, the entire equity in Harvard Heritage Sdn Bhd and a 51 percent stake in Keris Properties (PK) Sdn Bhd.
It also wanted to do a rights issue and a special issue for Bumiputra (ethnic Malay) investors.
The acquisition of Harvard and Keris and the special issue are additions to the company's previous proposals.
The company had sought to diversify its operations through the acquisitions, which would have taken it into property investment and development as well as stockbroking.
Perdana did not provide reasons for the rejection of the proposals.
